title: Layered oxide cathodes
text: Layered lithium transition-metal oxides such as LiCoO2, NMC, and NCA are widely studied battery cathodes. Their performance depends on lithium diffusion pathways, transition-metal redox chemistry, cation mixing, oxygen stability, and surface degradation during cycling.

title: Olivine lithium iron phosphate
text: LiFePO4 is an olivine phosphate cathode known for thermal stability, long cycle life, and relatively safe operation. Its lower electronic conductivity is commonly addressed through carbon coating, nanosizing, and conductive additives.

title: Sulfide solid electrolytes
text: Sulfide solid electrolytes can show high lithium-ion conductivity because their soft polarizable anion framework lowers migration barriers. Practical deployment must manage moisture sensitivity, interfacial reactions with electrodes, and mechanical compatibility.

title: Band gap and semiconductor selection
text: Band gap is a key descriptor for semiconductor applications. Wide band gap materials are useful for power electronics and ultraviolet optoelectronics, while moderate band gap semiconductors can be suitable for photovoltaics, photodetectors, and transistors.

title: Silicon and gallium arsenide
text: Silicon is abundant, mechanically robust, and central to integrated circuits. Gallium arsenide has a direct band gap and high electron mobility, making it valuable for optoelectronics and high-frequency devices despite higher cost and processing complexity.

title: Lightweight aerospace alloys
text: Aerospace alloy design often balances low density with high specific strength, fatigue resistance, oxidation resistance, and manufacturability. Aluminum, titanium, and magnesium alloys are common lightweight choices, with composition and heat treatment controlling precipitates and strength.

title: High entropy alloys
text: High entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements and can form simple solid-solution phases. Their properties may include high strength, fracture toughness, corrosion resistance, or thermal stability, depending on phase formation, lattice distortion, and chemical ordering.

title: Surface energy and catalytic behavior
text: Surface energy influences crystal morphology, surface stability, adsorption, and catalytic activity. Low-energy facets often dominate equilibrium shapes, while high-energy sites can be more reactive and important for catalytic transformations.

title: Thermoelectric materials
text: Thermoelectric performance is described by the figure of merit ZT, which depends on Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and temperature. Good thermoelectrics combine strong electronic transport with suppressed lattice thermal conductivity.

title: Perovskite stability
text: Perovskite materials can offer strong optical absorption and tunable band gaps, but stability against moisture, heat, light, ion migration, and interfacial reactions remains a central challenge for long-lived devices.

title: Mechanical moduli and hardness
text: Bulk modulus measures resistance to volume compression, while shear modulus measures resistance to shape change. High bulk and shear moduli often correlate with stiffness, hardness, and resistance to elastic deformation.

title: Energy above hull
text: Energy above hull estimates thermodynamic stability relative to competing phases. Materials on the convex hull are predicted stable, while small positive energy above hull values may indicate metastable compounds that can sometimes be synthesized.
